name: QOIR
baseline: libpng (Debian Bullseye build); also libwebp lossless (Debian Bullseye build) and libjxl lossless
workload: Lossless encode and decode of the QOI benchmark suite images (qoiformat.org benchmark tarball), single-threaded, megapixels per second plus compression ratio.
claimed_speedup: doc/full_benchmarks.txt: QOIR_Lossless 168.90 EncMPixels/s and 276.45 DecMPixels/s vs PNG/libpng 5.49 and 56.18 (about 31x encode and 4.9x decode, derived from page data; the README states 30x and 4.9x) and vs WebP_Lossless 2.49 and 89.94 (about 68x encode and 3.1x decode, derived from page data). Compression ratio 0.2525 vs libpng 0.2423 and WebP_Lossless 0.1651 (lower is better).
compiler_and_flags: gcc (Debian 10.2.1-6) 10.2.1; script/run_full_benchmarks.sh defaults to CFLAGS '-Wall -O3' and compiles the codec adapters with -march=native; libpng and libwebp are Debian Bullseye system builds (their build flags are not stated)
hardware: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10210U CPU @ 1.60GHz (desktop/laptop, single-threaded), Debian Bullseye
tradeoffs: Experimental, non-standard file format ('subject to incompatible changes' per README): no ecosystem outside the QOIR library, so files cannot be read by libpng, libwebp or browsers. Compresses worse than libpng and much worse than WebP lossless (0.2525 vs 0.2423 and 0.1651). Single-file C library (src/qoir.h), no dependencies, bundles its own LZ4; tiles allow multi-threaded decode. Lossless 24-bit RGB or 32-bit RGBA only, plus a trivial lossy mode.
caveats: Author's own benchmark, but the full script, adapters and raw output are public. Baselines are Debian system libpng and libwebp, so their compiler flags are unstated; one laptop-class CPU (i5-10210U) and gcc 10.2.1. In the same table Wuffs' PNG decoder decodes at 140.79 MPixels/s (vs libpng 56.18), and the README says ZPNG is 'very competitive with and sometimes strictly better than QOIR'. AVIF was not measured (author hit Debian bug 976349), so there is no libavif comparison. An independent suite (WangXuan95/Image-Compression-Benchmark, CLIC2021) also lists QOIR at 23.696 compress and 19.752 decompress vs Pillow PNG 334.791 and 33.677 (unit not stated on that page).
found_via: WebSearch 'fast PNG decoder encoder faster than libpng SIMD library site:github.com' (result nigeltao/qoir); opened README and doc/full_benchmarks.txt

name: fpng
workload: Encode and decode 24/32-bit PNG images; in the cited QOIR run, the QOI benchmark suite images, single-threaded, megapixels per second.
claimed_speedup: Independent run in doc/full_benchmarks.txt: PNG/fpng 192.16 EncMPixels/s and 148.19 DecMPixels/s vs PNG/libpng 5.49 and 56.18 (about 35x encode and 2.6x decode, derived from page data); compression ratio 0.3115 vs libpng 0.2423 (lower is better). fpng's own README separately claims 'about 23x faster compression, 2.5-3x faster decompression' than libpng.
compiler_and_flags: gcc (Debian 10.2.1-6) 10.2.1; script/run_full_benchmarks.sh defaults to CFLAGS '-Wall -O3' and compiles the codec adapters with -march=native; libpng and libwebp are Debian Bullseye system builds (their build flags are not stated); fpng's own README benchmarks used MSVC 2019 (flags not stated)
hardware: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10210U CPU @ 1.60GHz (desktop/laptop, single-threaded), Debian Bullseye; fpng README numbers were taken on a Xeon E5-2690 3.00 GHz
tradeoffs: The fast decoder only decodes PNG files written by fpng (it checks a private fdEC chunk and returns FPNG_DECODE_NOT_FPNG otherwise), so for arbitrary PNGs a general decoder such as libpng or Wuffs is still needed. Encoder uses only filter 2 and RLE-style matches of distance 3 or 4 with precomputed Huffman tables, so files are much larger than libpng (about 29% larger in the cited run). 24/32bpp only, SSE4.1+PCLMUL for the speed-ups, SIMD only on x86; public domain (Unlicense), so no patent grant.
caveats: The README's own table does not include libpng: its libpng claim is a prose line and its decode speed-up is measured on fpng-compressed PNGs only. The A tier comes from nigeltao/qoir's public benchmark script (one i5-10210U, gcc 10.2.1, Debian libpng). The decoder is limited to fpng's own output, which flatters decode numbers; the author recommends Wuffs for reading arbitrary PNGs.
found_via: WebSearch 'fast PNG decoder encoder faster than libpng SIMD library site:github.com' (result richgel999/fpng); opened README and cross-checked against nigeltao/qoir doc/full_benchmarks.txt

name: fpnge
workload: PNG encoding of the QOI benchmark suite images, single-threaded, megapixels per second (encoder only; no decoder).
claimed_speedup: doc/full_benchmarks.txt in nigeltao/qoir: PNG/fpnge 312.59 EncMPixels/s vs PNG/libpng 5.49 (about 57x, derived from page data); compression ratio 0.2798 vs libpng 0.2423 (lower is better). fpnge's own README only states 180 to 800 MP/s on a Threadripper 3970x.
compiler_and_flags: gcc (Debian 10.2.1-6) 10.2.1; script/run_full_benchmarks.sh defaults to CFLAGS '-Wall -O3' and compiles the codec adapters with -march=native; libpng and libwebp are Debian Bullseye system builds (their build flags are not stated)
hardware: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10210U CPU @ 1.60GHz (desktop/laptop, single-threaded), Debian Bullseye
stars_or_usage: 113 stars; also used as a PNG baseline in the QOIR benchmarks
tradeoffs: Encoder only (no decoder). Uses AVX2 and a fixed special Huffman table, so output is about 15% larger than libpng's (0.2798 vs 0.2423 in the cited run) and it is x86 AVX2 only (QOIR README notes no ARM SIMD). Supports 8 and 16 bit content, 1 to 4 channels, can emit cICP chunks for HDR. README calls it a 'proof-of-concept'.
caveats: The speed-up figure comes from a third party's benchmark (nigeltao/qoir), not from fpnge's README, which has no libpng comparison. One laptop-class CPU and gcc 10.2.1 in that run; baseline libpng is a Debian system build.
found_via: WebSearch 'fast PNG decoder encoder faster than libpng SIMD library site:github.com' and 'github PNG encoder decoder library C++ faster than libpng ...' (fpnge listed); opened README and nigeltao/qoir benchmarks

name: QOI (Quite OK Image format)
workload: Lossless encode and decode of the QOI benchmark suite images, single-threaded, megapixels per second (as measured by nigeltao/qoir).
claimed_speedup: doc/full_benchmarks.txt in nigeltao/qoir: QOI 146.87 EncMPixels/s and 193.53 DecMPixels/s vs PNG/libpng 5.49 and 56.18 (about 27x encode and 3.4x decode, derived from page data); compression ratio 0.2823 vs libpng 0.2423 (lower is better).
compiler_and_flags: gcc (Debian 10.2.1-6) 10.2.1; script/run_full_benchmarks.sh defaults to CFLAGS '-Wall -O3' and compiles the codec adapters with -march=native; libpng and libwebp are Debian Bullseye system builds (their build flags are not stated)
hardware: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10210U CPU @ 1.60GHz (desktop/laptop, single-threaded), Debian Bullseye
tradeoffs: Single-header C library under 700 lines. Output is about 16% larger than libpng's in the cited run and compresses far worse than WebP lossless; 8-bit RGB/RGBA only; non-standard format with limited tool support. Decoder is scalar; faster variants exist (see wx257osn2/qoixx).
caveats: The README of phoboslab/qoi itself has no numbers (it links to qoiformat.org/benchmark, which is egress-blocked here and was not opened); the evidence is the independent nigeltao/qoir run. The fpng README (richgel999/fpng) measured QOI at 83.90 and 138.18 MP/s but against stb_image and lodepng, not libpng. The Image-Compression-Benchmark suite (Pillow PNG, not libpng) lists QOI at 19.061 compress and 18.970 decompress vs PNG 334.791 and 33.677 (unit not stated).
found_via: Referenced by the QOIR README and fpng README opened under WebSearch 'fast PNG decoder encoder faster than libpng SIMD library site:github.com'; opened phoboslab/qoi README, Makefile and qoibench.c

name: Zpng
baseline: libpng (Debian Bullseye build); also libwebp lossless
workload: Lossless photographic image compression and decompression of the QOI benchmark suite images (nigeltao/qoir run), megapixels per second plus compression ratio.
claimed_speedup: doc/full_benchmarks.txt in nigeltao/qoir: ZPNG_Lossless 126.21 EncMPixels/s and 256.32 DecMPixels/s vs PNG/libpng 5.49 and 56.18 (about 23x encode and 4.6x decode, derived from page data) with smaller output (compression ratio 0.2182 vs libpng 0.2423, lower is better); vs WebP_Lossless 2.49 and 89.94 (about 51x encode and 2.8x decode, derived from page data), though WebP lossless is smaller (0.1651).
compiler_and_flags: gcc (Debian 10.2.1-6) 10.2.1; script/run_full_benchmarks.sh defaults to CFLAGS '-Wall -O3' and compiles the codec adapters with -march=native; libpng and libwebp are Debian Bullseye system builds (their build flags are not stated)
hardware: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10210U CPU @ 1.60GHz (desktop/laptop, single-threaded), Debian Bullseye
stars_or_usage: 312 stars; used as a comparison codec in QOIR and Image-Compression-Benchmark
tradeoffs: Not PNG: writes its own .zpng format (PNG-style filtering plus zstd), so files are not readable by libpng or browsers. Depends on the zstd library. Author calls it a small experimental library written in one evening (about 500 lines); 5 commits per the repo page and none since 2018. Focus is photographic images.
caveats: In the cited run the ZPNG code is upstream Zpng built through nigeltao/qoir's adapter. The Zpng README itself claims 'less than 6% of the time of a PNG compressor and a file that is 66% of the size' (248.737 ms vs 4339.82 ms on one JPEG-derived image), without naming the PNG library. Image-Compression-Benchmark (CLIC2021, i7-12700H, Windows 10, Pillow PNG not libpng) lists ZPNG at 25.909 compress and 24.083 decompress vs PNG 334.791 and 33.677 (unit not stated).
found_via: Named in nigeltao/qoir README (opened) from WebSearch 'fast PNG decoder encoder faster than libpng SIMD library site:github.com'; opened Zpng README and the Image-Compression-Benchmark README

name: libspng
workload: PNG decode of six images (19k 8bpp, 40k 24bpp, 77k 8bpp, 552k 32bpp, 4002k 24bpp) in the Wuffs benchmark harness, MB/s of decoded output.
claimed_speedup: Wuffs blog appendix (third-party measurement): libspng decodes 1.02x to 1.62x faster than libpng, for example libspng_decode_552k_32bpp_ignore_checksum/clang9 236MB/s vs libpng 146MB/s (1.62x) and libspng_decode_40k_24bpp/gcc10 77.5MB/s vs libpng 73.1MB/s (1.06x). The libspng README claims it 'outperforms the reference implementation in common use cases' with a chart image only.
compiler_and_flags: clang 9 and gcc 10 (flags not stated in the appendix)
tradeoffs: C library with an API incompatible with libpng. Feature gaps: animated PNG only planned; gamma correction not implemented for some output formats and some G8/GA8/GA16 conversions are not supported. Code is BSD-2-Clause but contains libpng-derived optimizations and test images under the PNG Reference Library License v2. Can build against miniz instead of zlib.
caveats: Numbers come from the Wuffs author's blog (the Wuffs harness code is public, but the post does not state the CPU model, so tier B rather than A) against Debian's system libpng; the gain is modest and image-dependent (1.02x on small 8bpp images). The same blog shows libpng with zlib-ng is 1.01x to 1.21x faster than stock libpng, which narrows the gap. mango's README (t0rakka/mango, i7-11800H, 2560x1600) lists spng at 37.7 ms decode and 215.9 ms encode vs libpng 57.3 ms and 820.5 ms, consistent with a 1.5x decode and 3.8x encode gain (derived from page data).
found_via: WebSearch 'lossless image codec faster than libwebp lossless PNG encoder decoder C++ github benchmark' surfaced the Wuffs blog; its appendix lists libspng; confirmed with the libspng README

name: mango
baseline: libpng; libjpeg (variant not stated in README, possibly libjpeg-turbo)
workload: Decode and encode single large PNG and JPEG images (PNG 2560x1600 and 4833x5875; JPEG 5184x3456 and 2560x1600), milliseconds per image plus output size.
claimed_speedup: README tables: PNG decode 3.2 ms vs libpng 57.3 ms (2560x1600) and 53.7 ms vs 379.5 ms (4833x5875); PNG encode 57.2 ms vs 820.5 ms and 287.0 ms vs 14051.3 ms; JPEG decode 23.3 ms vs libjpeg 197.8 ms (5184x3456) and 3.2 ms vs 32.9 ms (2560x1600); JPEG encode 18.5 ms vs 70.1 ms and 4.3 ms vs 16.3 ms. That is about 18x PNG decode and 8.5x JPEG decode on the first image of each pair (derived from page data).
hardware: PNG tables: 11th Gen Intel Core i7-11800H @ 2.30GHz; JPEG tables: Intel Core i9 8950HK @ 2.90GHz
tradeoffs: Large C++20 graphics library (SIMD vector math, virtual filesystem, thread pool, Vulkan text) of which the codecs are one part; adopting only the codecs means pulling a big dependency. Output is larger than the baselines in the README tables (PNG 3531 KB vs libpng 2843 KB; JPEG 6925 KB vs libjpeg 6677 KB at the larger sizes). Recent work includes HDR PNG and UltraHDR JPEG decoding; latest commits touch the NEON and SSE iDCT.
caveats: Compiler, flags and thread count are not stated; the mango README has a thread pool section, so the gap may include multi-threading against single-threaded baselines (unverified). The JPEG baseline is just 'libjpeg' and an 8.5x decode lead over a SIMD-enabled libjpeg-turbo would be unusually large, so it may be plain IJG libjpeg. The two table pairs use different CPUs. First-party numbers only; no benchmark program was inspected. Source license file is zlib-style custom text with a 'MANGO' copyright header; bundled third-party code was not audited.
found_via: Prior knowledge of C++ image libraries (not surfaced by a search query); opened the t0rakka/mango github.com page, README, license and commits page

name: ptpng
baseline: libpng with zlib-ng 2.2.4 (ZLIB_COMPAT); for the encoder also stock zlib level 6 and zlib-ng level 6
workload: PNG decode (27 cases across native, RGB8 and RGBA8 output) and encode (nine generated fixtures: gradients, graphics, noise) on five CI platforms, median of alternating rounds.
claimed_speedup: README: decoder geometric-mean speedup over libpng + zlib-ng 2.2.4 across 27 cases is 1.80x Linux x64, 1.64x Windows x64, 1.59x Linux ARM64, 1.62x macOS ARM64 and 1.46x Windows ARM64 (30 Sep 2026 run). Encoder (after 1 Oct change) averages 2.25-2.98x stock zlib level 6 and 1.14-1.52x zlib-ng, with files at most 2.4% larger than zlib-ng level 6.
compiler_and_flags: CMake Release build; nightly workflow matrix uses gcc, clang and MSVC cl (versions not stated); PERFORMANCE.md quotes -O3 for paired runs and MSVC /O2 for one local run
hardware: AMD EPYC 7763 (Windows x64 runner, four logical CPUs) for the 30 Sep snapshot; Intel i7-1355U for local runs; Neoverse-N2 for Linux ARM64 (PERFORMANCE.md)
tradeoffs: No LICENSE file found at the repo root (raw.githubusercontent.com returned 404 for LICENSE, LICENSE.md and LICENSE.txt) and the README has no license section, so reuse rights are unclear. Single-threaded; library calls must be serialized across threads (shared tables and dispatch state). Encoder writes non-interlaced PNG without palette, packed-sample or metadata support. C11 core with a header-only C++17/20 wrapper; AVX2/SSE2 on x86 and NEON on ARM64.
caveats: Very new repository (0 stars; commit activity visible from 2026-09-24 and PERFORMANCE.md is titled 'September-October 2026'); numbers change nightly and the README says compare ratios only within a run. Fixtures are synthetic (gradients, graphics, random noise) and the project itself says they do not establish a fastest-in-the-world claim. Decoder loses on some Windows cases (26/27) and the new encoder loses to zlib-ng level 6 in several fixtures (for example 0.76x on photo_rgb8 in the local i7-1355U table per PERFORMANCE.md). Compiler versions are not stated, so a verifier who finds them in CI logs could promote this to tier A.
found_via: WebSearch 'fast PNG decoder encoder faster than libpng SIMD library site:github.com' (result bojosos/ptpng); opened README, PERFORMANCE.md, CI workflows and commits page

name: lodepng-turbo
workload: Baseline PNG decompression using SIMD filters and libdeflate in place of zlib (no workload described).
claimed_speedup: README: 'On x86 and x86-64 or ARM systems, lodepng-turbo is twice as fast as libpng, but it may be slower elsewhere.' No numbers beyond 'twice as fast'.
tradeoffs: Hacked lodepng with libdeflate (git submodule, builds with gcc/clang and GNU make) plus 'depng' prediction routines for unfiltering; accelerates decoding only. Implements both the lodepng API and a TurboPNG API. README itself warns it 'may be slower elsewhere'.
caveats: No benchmark program, methodology, CPU, compiler or data in the repository; the single ratio is first-party. Repository has had no commits since January 2019, so numbers predate current libpng (which has its own SIMD) and libdeflate. The predecessor repository kanryu/simd_lode_png states a goal of 5x libpng but contains no measurements.
found_via: WebSearch 'fast PNG decoder encoder faster than libpng SIMD library site:github.com' (result kanryu/lodepng-turbo); opened README and commits page

name: pngenc
workload: Encode one 1920x1080 24-bit image to PNG in three low-compression modes (uncompressed, Huffman-only, RLE).
claimed_speedup: README table (ms, libpng 1.6 vs pngenc 1 thread vs pngenc multi-threaded): Uncompressed 9 vs 0.8 vs 0.2; Huffman Only 82 vs 7.3 vs 1.2; RLE 84 vs 30 vs 4. README says 'up to an order of magnitude faster' at the same compression rates in those modes.
tradeoffs: Encoder only. Supports only uncompressed, Huffman-only and RLE modes (full LZ77 is 'N/A'), so it does not replace libpng at default compression levels. Needs OpenMP for the multi-threaded numbers; tested with gcc/mingw, clang and MSVC. Author calls it a hobby project; the CRC32 code is adapted from Mark Adler under a zlib-compatible license.
caveats: Single first-party table, one image and one CPU; compiler, flags and benchmark harness are not stated. The comparison is against libpng's low-effort strategies (Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY, Z_RLE) which the README itself calls a valid trade-off. No libpng-at-default-level comparison is given for any mode that pngenc supports.
found_via: WebSearch 'fast PNG decoder encoder faster than libpng SIMD library site:github.com' (result GregorBudweiser/pngenc); opened readme.md, LICENSE and commits page

name: ImageZero
workload: Lossless compression and decompression of 24-bit PPM files, natural photos.
claimed_speedup: README: 'Compared to PNG, it compresses 24 bit PPM files about 20 times faster, and decompresses to PPM about 2 times faster, while the compression rate is nearly as good as PNG for natural photos.'
tradeoffs: Own format and API (README calls it 'early work in progress'; neither format nor API fully outlined). Works on 24-bit RGB only; README says it is not suited for flat computer-generated graphics or grayscale images.
caveats: Only a README paragraph: no benchmark code, images, CPU, compiler, flags or PNG library version, so the baseline is inferred (low confidence). Repository has had no commits since 2013, so the comparison predates modern libpng and zlib-ng. Found in the GitHub topic listings for image-compression and image-decoder; I did not open a second benchmark page.
found_via: github.com/topics/image-compression?l=c%2B%2B and github.com/topics/image-decoder?l=c%2B%2B (cfeck/imagezero listed as 'Fast Lossless Color Image Compression Library'); opened the README and commits page

name: qoixx
workload: QOI encode and decode of the QOI benchmark suite (grand total, 20 iterations), ms and megapixels per second, on seven CPUs.
claimed_speedup: README: on Intel Core i9-10900 (g++ 11.1.0) qoi decodes in 2.2389 ms (207.326 mpps) and encodes in 2.5434 ms (182.504 mpps) vs qoixx 1.3477 ms (344.431 mpps) and 1.5255 ms (304.280 mpps), about 1.7x faster in both directions (derived from page data); similar gains on Ryzen 7 2700X, Ryzen 7 3800X, Ryzen 9 3950X, AWS Graviton3, Kryo 585 and Apple M1 Max.
compiler_and_flags: g++ versions listed per CPU, 11.0.0 to 12.0.0 (11.1.0 on the i9-10900); optimization flags not stated
hardware: Intel Core i9-10900; AMD Ryzen 7 2700X; Ryzen 7 3800X; Ryzen 9 3950X; AWS Graviton3; Qualcomm Kryo 585; Apple M1 Max
tradeoffs: Single-header C++20 QOI codec with SIMD encoder (AVX2, SVE or NEON, scalar fallback via QOIXX_NO_SIMD). Decoder is optimized scalar and 'with some input, original implementation is faster'. Output size is identical to qoi.h (463 KB total). Decoder built with MSVC is not fast per the FAQ.
caveats: Baseline is qoi.h, not libpng/libwebp, so this only qualifies indirectly: see the QOI entry for qoi.h vs libpng (about 27x encode, 3.4x decode in nigeltao/qoir's run). Optimization flags and benchmark program are not stated in the README; first-party numbers.
found_via: github.com/topics/image-compression?l=c%2B%2B (wx257osn2/qoixx listed as 'Single Header Quite Fast QOI Implementation written in C++20'); opened README, LICENSE and commits page

name: libjxl fast_lossless (FJXL) encoder
baseline: libpng (Debian Bullseye build); libwebp lossless (Debian Bullseye build)
workload: Lossless encode of the QOI benchmark suite images with libjxl's fast_lossless (FJXL, AVX2) encoder and decode with the regular libjxl decoder, megapixels per second plus compression ratio.
claimed_speedup: doc/full_benchmarks.txt in nigeltao/qoir: JXL_Lossless/f 106.48 EncMPixels/s vs PNG/libpng 5.49 (about 19x) and WebP_Lossless 2.49 (about 43x), both derived from page data; compression ratio 0.2171 vs libpng 0.2423 and WebP_Lossless 0.1651 (lower is better). Decode is slower: 33.16 DecMPixels/s vs libpng 56.18 and WebP_Lossless 89.94.
compiler_and_flags: gcc (Debian 10.2.1-6) 10.2.1; script/run_full_benchmarks.sh defaults to CFLAGS '-Wall -O3' and compiles the codec adapters with -march=native; libpng and libwebp are Debian Bullseye system builds (their build flags are not stated); the JXL adapter is built with -DFASTLL_ENABLE_AVX2_INTRINSICS=1 against libjxl built per its README
hardware: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10210U CPU @ 1.60GHz (desktop/laptop, single-threaded), Debian Bullseye
tradeoffs: Applies to the fast_lossless encoder inside libjxl (lib/jxl/enc_fast_lossless.h, standalone or in-library mode), not libjxl at its default effort 7, which encodes at 0.57 MPixels/s in the same table. Files are readable only by JPEG XL decoders; decode is slower than libpng and libwebp; AVX2 path for the speed (FASTLL_ENABLE_AVX2_INTRINSICS); large dependency footprint when using the full library.
caveats: The measured speed-up is for the encoder only and the table is a third party's (nigeltao/qoir); libjxl's own README has no speed numbers. The same table shows regular libjxl lossless at effort 3 (5.35 MP/s) and effort 7 (0.57 MP/s) is not faster than libpng at encode. Baselines are Debian system builds with unstated flags. No libavif comparison.
found_via: Named as 'JXL_Lossless/f' in nigeltao/qoir doc/full_benchmarks.txt; github.com/topics/jpeg?l=c%2B%2B listed libjxl; opened lib/jxl/enc_fast_lossless.h, commits page

name: Grok JPEG 2000 codec
baseline: OpenJPEG (JPEG 2000); also Kakadu (proprietary, via GDAL JP2KAK)
workload: GDAL workflows reading JPEG 2000 imagery: Spot 6 on network storage, Spot 6 on local storage, and a Pleiades region read, using 16 threads and a GDAL release build.
claimed_speedup: README table (Grok JP2Grok vs Kakadu JP2KAK vs OpenJPEG): Spot 6 (Network Storage) 35.17 s vs 344 s vs 85 s; Spot 6 (Local Storage) 26.92 s vs 30.57 s vs 52.09 s; Pleiades (Region) 0.74 s vs 1.41 s vs 4.28 s.
compiler_and_flags: GDAL release build (compiler and flags not stated)
tradeoffs: Strong copyleft: AGPL v3 (network use triggers source obligations), a poor fit for permissive-license projects. Adds HTJ2K, random-access sub-image decoding with TLM and PLT markers, a multi-level tile cache and S3 access, which are features of the whole GDAL workflow measured. Reported to have started as an OpenJPEG fork (per third-party descriptions seen in search snippets); GitHub does not mark it as a fork.
caveats: JPEG 2000 is outside the listed baselines (libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp, libavif); OpenJPEG is the widely used open-source incumbent. First-party end-to-end GDAL timings that include I/O, caching and region reads, not codec-only throughput. CPU model, compiler flags and the benchmark inputs are not given in the README. Kakadu's 344 s network-storage result is far above its 30.57 s local result, which suggests an I/O-pattern effect rather than codec speed (my inference).
found_via: WebSearch 'JPEG 2000 HTJ2K codec C++ "faster than OpenJPEG" github' (result listing Grok); opened README, LICENSE and commits page

name: CharLS
baseline: Pillow PNG encoder and Pillow JPEG 2000 plugin (in Image-Compression-Benchmark); the README compares against the original HP JPEG-LS code, JPEG-XR and JPEG 2000
workload: Lossless compression and decompression of 585 CLIC2021 RGB 24-bit images (4.1 GB), single-threaded, total time and total size, using the CharLS-based pillow-jpls 1.3.2 plugin.
claimed_speedup: Image-Compression-Benchmark (CLIC2021, units not stated on page, presumably seconds): JPEG-LS compress 72.237 and decompress 66.567 vs JPEG2000 319.912 and 275.398 (about 4.4x and 4.1x faster, derived from page data) and vs PNG (optimize=False) 334.791 and 33.677 (4.6x faster compress but about 2x slower decompress); JPEG-LS total size 1931584595 vs JPEG2000 1992860964 and PNG 2003016524 bytes. CharLS README: 'about twice as fast as the original HP code, and beats both JPEG-XR and JPEG 2000 by a factor 3'.
compiler_and_flags: Python 3.9 with Pillow 10.1.0 and pillow-jpls 1.3.2 (CharLS wheel build flags not stated)
tradeoffs: JPEG-LS (ISO/IEC 14495-1) is a lossless/near-lossless codec with low complexity; decode is about twice as slow as Pillow's PNG decode in the cited suite. README notes Hewlett Packard patents on JPEG-LS (licensed free for conformant implementations; some may have expired). No SIMD: speed comes from templates and traits.
caveats: Weak fit to the listed baselines: none of libjpeg-turbo, libpng, libwebp or libavif is directly compared, and Pillow's PNG codec uses zlib rather than libpng. The suite measures a Python wrapper (pillow-jpls, which PyPI says is based on CharLS), so Python overhead is included. The README's own 'twice as fast as HP code' claim cites a page on imagecompression.info that was not opened and is dated. Another JPEG-LS-family row ('JPEG-LS-ext') is a different codec and is not counted here.
found_via: github.com/topics/image-compression?l=c%2B%2B (team-charls/charls listed); opened README, LICENSE.md, commits page, the Image-Compression-Benchmark README and the pillow-jpls PyPI page
